newsitem.title: USA: ADR REPORT - Foreign shares fall with Dow.
newsitem.headline: ADR REPORT - Foreign shares fall with Dow.

text.p: Foreign shares fell with the Dow Tuesday as fears about a hike in U.S. interest rates spooked investors and triggered a pullback.
Traders said a senior Fed official's comments to Reuters rattled investors, who were already nervous after the U.S. market's recent rally.
"We're all trading in line with the Dow," one said. "Everybody knows the market's pretty fully valued here, and I think what you're seeing are emotional movements."

The unidentified Fed official said eight of the 12 district banks in the Federal Reserve System requested a hike in the five percent discount rate. Of those eight, three asked for a 50-basis-point rise, the official told Reuters.
The Dow was down 17.76, or 0.30 percent, to 5,871.44 in early afternoon trade, putting pressure on American Depositary Receipts (ADRs).
Alcatel Alsthom lost 3/8 to 14-1/4, Rhone Poulenc shed 1/4 to 27-1/8, Telefonica de Espana lost 3/4 to 56-1/4, Royal Dutch fell 2-5/8 to 154-7/8, and British Petroleum retreated 1-1/4 to 120-3/4.
News Corp retreated 1/4 to 20-7/8, and Hong Kong Telecom slipped 1/8 to 17.

Semiconductor-related stocks managed to buck the trend, however, surging on the back of Intel's bullish outlook for its third quarter revenues. SGS-Thomson jumped over five percent, rising 2-1/4 to 46-1/4, while Philips Electronics added two percent, gaining 3/4 to 34.

B.A.T Industries was also stronger, rising with other tobacco stocks in the U.S. after news that a judge dismissed pre-1994 claims in a Medical lawsuit brought against the industry by the state of Florida.
In other activity, Latin American shares were flat to weaker in thin trade on the back of the Dow's softness.
Mexico's Telmex was flat at 32-1/2, Televisa slid 1/8 to 29-1/2, Brazil's Telebras shed 1/8 to 78-3/4, and Argentina's YPF lost 1/4 to 22-5/8.
Chile's CTC inched up 1/8 to 98-7/8, and Telefonica del Peru held steady at 22-7/8.
